context: Before rotation, subtree root 5 has left child 3 and right child 6. Node 3 has left child 1 and right child 4, and node 1 has only left child 0. The figure labels unbalanced node 5 as node, its left child 3 as child, and the right child of 3, node 4, as grand_child.

The balance factor is the left subtree height minus the right subtree height. An empty subtree has height −1 and a leaf has height 0. The connections give root 5 left and right subtree heights 2 and 0. Its balance factor is 2, so it needs a right rotation.
description: The right rotation promotes left child 3 to subtree root and makes the old root 5 its right child. The original right child of 3 is grandchild 4, so save the reference to 4 first and transfer it to the left of 5 during the rotation. Since 3 < 4 < 5, node 4 is still in the right subtree of 3 and to the left of 5. The binary search tree ordering is preserved.

Update the references in order: save grand_child = child.right, then set child.right = node, and finally set node.left = grand_child. Node 1 and its left child 0 stay on the left of 3, and node 6 remains the right child of 5.

From left to right, the three panels show the tree before rotation, after the right rotation and grandchild transfer, and with the layout adjusted. All actual connections are in place in the middle panel. Pale dashed marks at the old positions of 5 and 6 and their old edges are for comparison. The final panel simply removes them and adjusts the layout. There is no second rotation.
prose.result: All nodes are retained, and the inorder sequence is still [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6].
